research_question: What is the effect of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA, DHA or combinations), compared with placebo, on quality of life at the end of treatment in adults with major depressive disorder?
treatment_label: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA, DHA, or combinations)
outcome_description: Quality of life measured by any validated scale (such as SF-36, Q-LES-Q, or WHOQOL) at the end of treatment
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater improvement or higher quality of life favoring omega-3 fatty acids over placebo
search_queries: omega-3 fatty acids major depressive disorder quality of life randomized trial
EPA DHA depression quality of life controlled trial
fish oil depression SF-36 trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder receiving omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA, DHA, or combination) compared with a placebo control
Original empirical studies reporting quantitative quality-of-life outcomes using a validated measurement instrument at the end of treatment
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols)
No comparison between omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and a placebo control group
No quantitative outcome data on quality of life allowing calculation of an effect size (means and standard deviations, standard errors, change scores, or test statistics)
Studies in populations without major depressive disorder or completely unrelated to omega-3 supplementation
moderators_to_extract: Omega-3 composition/formulation (EPA-pure/predominant vs DHA-pure/predominant vs balanced)
Daily dose of omega-3 (mg/day of EPA and DHA)
Treatment setting (monotherapy vs adjunctive to standard antidepressants)
Quality of life instrument used (e.g., SF-36, Q-LES-Q, WHOQOL)
effect_size_note: Standardized mean difference (Hedges g) for continuous quality-of-life scale scores at end of treatment.
